question: Who led the Battle of Plassey on behalf of the British East India Company?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Clive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Battle of Plassey:

 
 
• It was fought in 1757 in the Plassey region of West Bengal, on the east of the Bhagirathi river. 
 
• Troops of the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, came up against the forces of Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last independent Nawab of Bengal, and his French allies.
 
• The victory of the British East India Company in the Battle of Plassey is one of the important landmarks in India History. 
 
• The Battle of Plassey paved the way for the beginning of the British empire in India.
 
• The British enjoyed the tax benefits, had to compete with no rival foreign merchants, and began to use the revenue of Bengal for protecting their military and trade interests.
 
• So much wealth was drained from Bengal that the economy was completely shattered. This is known as the Plassey Plunder.
 
• With the wealth of Bengal, the British secured their business and political supremacy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Governor and company of merchants of London trading into the East Indies, popularly known as the English East India Company, were formed in 1600 AD. 
 
• Captain William Hawkins arrived at Jahangir’s court in 1609 AD to seek permission to open a factory in Surat.
 
 
• A Farman was issued by Jahangir, permitting the English to build a factory in Surat.
 
 
 
• In 1613, a permanent factory of East India Company was established at Surat.
 
• In 1611, the company established its first factory in the south in Masulipattanam.
